audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven rows contradicted their own why. Level 1 read Lillia under 'it's an even farm stage'; levels 2, 3 and 4-5 read Skill/Tahm Kench under whys that describe you grinding him down ('your best lane stretch'); level 6 read Lillia under 'the solo lane is just even here'. diff also read EVEN against diffRating 4/10, green tone and breakdown.difficulty 'Favoured'.
audit.why: The packet chart reads Skill / Lillia / Lillia / Lillia / Skill / Tahm Kench / Tahm Kench, which matches the prose on every row.
audit.corrected: Rows 0 through 4 proposed as matched full+content pairs onto the packet chart, ratings adjusted, diff set to FAV.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item and 2+ item whys in the full layer promised melted tanks and teamfight dominance on rows scored Tahm Kench.
audit.why: His item spike is Thick Skin plus Heartsteel — the grey health banks exactly the damage-over-time Lillia deals, which is the one profile that beats her burn.
audit.corrected: phases[5].why and phases[6].why rewritten around Thick Skin and the three-stack stun.

audit.whatIsWrong: Tahm Kench's kit was mislabelled throughout. The page credits 'W self-heal' (the heal is on Tongue Lash, Q), 'W devour' (Devour is R), 'grey-health passive' (grey health is Thick Skin, E) and calls his Q a 'point-blank tongue stun' (it is 900 range). Worst of all, it never says the stun is conditional.
audit.why: Tongue Lash only stuns when you already carry three stacks of An Acquired Taste, built by him damaging you. That makes the stun countable and avoidable, which is the single most useful thing a Lillia can know here — and the page instead implies every Q is a stun. It also claims his R lets him 'roam and gank from across the map'; Devour does not travel.
audit.corrected: Every ability restored to its real slot, the three-stack condition stated in report[5].t, early, late, whys[6] and wants.foe[1], the 900 range given, and the R-roam claim replaced with Abyssal Dive's 1000-1200 range engage on 21/20/19/18/17s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags zero sequencing cues, and the page's tracked ability had no number attached.
audit.why: Abyssal Dive at 21s rank 1 is the longest cooldown in his kit and his only engage; that is the whole green light.
audit.corrected: Number added to dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, report[5].t and mid.

edits.after: Lullaby is online, but the drowsy delay only converts with a jungler — the solo lane stays level here.

edits.after: Thick Skin banks your burn as grey health and heals it back, and Heartsteel out-scales your DoT rotation.

edits.before: You're a teamfight nightmare now: sleep two, kite the rest, and let the burn do the bookkeeping.
edits.after: Three An Acquired Taste stacks turn his next Tongue Lash into a stun — and that stun ends you.

edits.before: His escape and re-engage — all-in only while it is down. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Abyssal Dive is 21s at rank 1 and it is his only engage — while it is down, every ring is free.

edits.before: Tahm Kench whiffs Abyssal Dive and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Abyssal Dive whiffs and you own the next twenty seconds of lane.

edits.before: Track Tahm Kench’s Abyssal Dive: His escape and re-engage — all-in only while it is down. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Track Abyssal Dive (21s at rank 1) for the engage — but the kill comes from An Acquired Taste: at three stacks his next Tongue Lash stuns you.

edits.before: You layer Q sweetspot with the E slow and start Dream Dust — the burn ticks faster than his early W heal can claw back, and your move speed keeps you off his Q stun.
edits.after: You layer Q sweetspot with the E slow and start Dream Dust — the burn ticks faster than Tongue Lash's heal claws back, and move speed keeps you out of its 900 range.

edits.before: His grey health and W self-heal come item-backed (Heartsteel) and out-last your entire DoT rotation — he soaks the burn and walks it off.
edits.after: Thick Skin banks your damage as grey health and Heartsteel backs it, so his shield out-lasts your whole DoT rotation — he walks the burn off.

edits.before: Tahm out-sustains and out-roams you: one Q tongue stun into W devour deletes a squishy Lillia, and his R snowballs the map while your damage greys away.
edits.after: Tahm out-sustains you: three An Acquired Taste stacks turn his next Tongue Lash into a stun, and Devour finishes a squishy Lillia while your damage greys away.

edits.before: Once Tahm has Heartsteel/grey-health stacking online, his W devour and self-heal out-last your entire DoT rotation — his takeover.
edits.after: Once Heartsteel and Thick Skin's grey health are online, his shield and the Tongue Lash heal out-last your whole DoT rotation — his takeover.

edits.before: Tahm's whole early game is grey health and W self-heal — every Dream Dust tick and Q sweetspot you land, his passive converts to grey and W's lifesteal claws it back, so single pokes do nothing. Your only real opening is Levels 2-3: layer Q sweetspot + E slow to start the burn and force HIM to walk into your hops, because the stacking move speed keeps you out of his Q tongue range. Never throw a hop in range of a point-blank Q stun — a single stun into his W devour bursts you out of the game.
edits.after: Tahm's early game is Thick Skin and the Tongue Lash heal — every Dream Dust tick and Q sweetspot you land gets banked as grey health and clawed back, so single pokes do nothing. Your opening is levels 2-3: layer Q sweetspot and the E slow to start the burn and force HIM to walk into your hops, because stacking move speed keeps you outside Tongue Lash's 900 range. Count his passive — damaging you stacks An Acquired Taste, and at three stacks his next Q stuns instead of slowing. That stun into Devour is what kills you.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your window: full-rank Q plus the compounding Dream Dust DoT means a Kench who has to step up to CS is bleeding the whole time, and your E slow + Q move speed make you uncatchable when he commits. Stack the burn from range and refuse to all-in — you can't out-trade his W heal in a straight fight, you out-tempo him by chipping and kiting. At 6 your Lilting Lullaby can sleep him through a step-up, but the delay is so long it only converts with a jungler; solo, treat R as anti-engage, not a kill button.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your window: full-rank Q plus the compounding Dream Dust DoT means a Kench who has to step up to CS bleeds the whole time, and your E slow and Q move speed make you uncatchable when he commits. Stack the burn from range and refuse to all-in — you can't out-trade the Tongue Lash heal in a straight fight; you out-tempo him by chipping and kiting. Abyssal Dive is 21s at rank 1, so his engage window is rare. At 6 Lullaby only converts with a jungler; solo, treat R as anti-engage.

edits.before: This is where Tahm reclaims everything. Once his grey-health and W devour are item-backed, his self-sustain simply out-lasts your full DoT rotation — you'll burn him to half and watch it grey back up. His R lets him roam and gank from across the map, and a single Q tongue stun on you in a teamfight means W devour and you're deleted. Don't try to 1v1 him late; use your Q move speed and sleep to peel and pick squishier targets, and pray you converted your 4-to-first-item tempo into a lead before his sustain came fully online.
edits.after: This is where Tahm reclaims everything. Once Thick Skin is item-backed his shield simply out-lasts your full DoT rotation — you burn him to half and watch it grey back up. In a fight the danger is the stack count: at three An Acquired Taste stacks his next Tongue Lash stuns from 900 range, and Devour finishes it. Abyssal Dive is what puts him on top of you from 1200 range with a knockup. Don't 1v1 him late; use your move speed and sleep to peel and pick softer targets, and hope you cashed your early tempo first.

notes: The mirror (tahmkench__lillia) reports that Lillia's full layer calls her 'him' throughout — breakdown.trading, breakdown.feeding, breakdown.late, dosFull[1].d and the report[] copies. I did not fix those here because rewriting them for pronoun alone risks the length band on strings I had no factual reason to touch; it is a champion-wide defect better handled by one sweep. The kit lists Devour's cooldown as 0 and its range as 25000, which are clearly the ally-cast values rather than the enemy-devour ones, so I quoted no number for it.
